title: Dedicated capacity: ramp/decay traffic profile & latency guardrails
creator: Anjali Rao
description:
Goal: Build and validate a ramp-and-decay load profile and latency guardrail checks for Dedicated pools that exercises autoscaler decision boundaries while tracking tokens/sec, p95 latency, and regression signals. This ticket implements the scenario, integrates p95 heatmaps into the console dashboard, and wires regression detector alerts to PagerDuty via the existing stability-sentinel.

Background: Current soak/burst suites cover steady bursts and long soaks but miss realistic traffic ramps where sustained throughput increases over tens of minutes followed by gradual decay. These ramp/decay patterns expose issues in autoscaler hysteresis, KV cache warmup, and tail-latency amplification. We need an automated harness that produces repeatable ramps, captures per-route p95 over sliding windows, and fails CI if regressions exceed defined thresholds.

Success criteria (acceptance criteria):
- Harness can produce traffic profiles: warmup (10m), linear-ramp (30m to +3x tokens/sec), plateau (20m), decay (30m).
- p95 latency SLO for target models: <= 220ms at baseline throughput, <= 600ms during peak plateau for medium-sized models.
- Regression detector triggers if p95 increases >25% relative to baseline for two consecutive runs or absolute p95 > 800ms for >5 minutes.
- Console dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 heatmap and tokens/sec vs target load in near-real-time (30s refresh).
- Test artifacts (raw traces, kernel-selection logs, KV cache hit rates) stored in the load-test bucket and linked to the ticket automatically.
- CI block PRs that cause regression detector failure for dedicated capacity regressions marked as P0.

Non-goals: full e2e customer-facing traffic replay, autoscaler policy changes (this ticket observes and reports), large-scale cost modeling (separate Optimize follow-up).
runbook_steps:
1) Provision test Dedicated pool (test-dedicated-ramp-01) with same instance types as staging.
2) Deploy model variants: baseline (v1.18-quant), fallback (v1.17), and small-quant to exercise fallbacks.
3) Start traffic generator that emits requests with token distribution matching chat workloads (mean 64 tokens, heavy tail to 1024).
4) Execute profile: warmup 10m at 0.7x, linear ramp 30m to 3x, plateau 20m, linear decay 30m. Repeat 3 runs.
5) Collect metrics: tokens/sec (per-second), p50/p95/p99 per-route, KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization, queue lengths, kernel switches.
6) Run regression-detector job comparing this run to baseline: compute relative p95 deltas and absolute thresholds.
7) If detector flags, attach traces and open ENG parent ticket for triage; send PD alert to #dedicated-stability and PagerDuty.
8) Clean up pool and archive artifacts to gs://redwood-load-tests/dedicated/ramp-ENG-56521/
setup_notes:
- Reuse traffic generator from ENG-31204, add new profile module 'ramp_decay'.
- Ensure tokenization mirrors production tokenizer (tokenizer-v2).
- Increase Prometheus retention for test namespace to 48h to allow drift analysis.
- Use a shadowing toggle to route 10% of production-like traffic into test pool when validating in staging.
- Add sampling on kernel selection logs to avoid exceeding logging quotas.
metrics_and_thresholds:
- Baseline throughput: 18k tokens/sec per GPU pool node (avg).
- Target ramp top: 54k tokens/sec (3x).
- p95 baseline target: <= 220ms.
- p95 plateau soft target: <= 600ms.
- Hard fail thresholds: p95 > 800ms for >5m OR relative p95 increase >25% over baseline in 2 consecutive runs.
- KV cache cold-start penalty: allowed up to +150ms p95 for first 10 minutes of warmup but must decay thereafter.
- Alerting: a single hard fail creates a PagerDuty incident, a soft/regression opens a Slack alert to #dedicated-stability.
updates: 2026-02-21 — Design review: aligned with PM and SRE on thresholds; decided to allow short KV cold-start penalty during warmup.
2026-02-26 — Prototype runner: traffic-generator 'ramp_decay' merged in PR 1287 (infra). Smoke runs in staging show expected throughput ramp shape.
2026-03-02 — Metrics ingestion: added p95 sliding-window computation (5m window with 1m step) and dashboard heatmap tile; Grafana panel patched.

2026-03-05 — Regression detector: implemented comparator that calculates both absolute and relative deltas; integrated with alerting rules. Test detector flagged benign kernel change; triaged with runtime team.

2026-03-10 — Running first full 3x ramp trial against test-dedicated-ramp-01. Observed p95 spike at 18m into ramp tied to KV warmup; artifacts uploaded for analysis. Next: tune autoscaler cooldown and test hysteresis settings.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Early traffic generator rate-limiter interactions may create artificial backpressure; mitigation: validate generator output at ingress with passive sampling.
- Risk: Logging volume from kernel traces could hit quotas; mitigation: sample traces and compress before upload.
- Risk: Autoscaler oscillation when exposed to linear ramps; mitigation: test with incremental cooldown adjustments and compare node add/remove timelines.
- Risk: False-positive regression detection after kernel optimization landings; mitigation: add whitelist for known runtime change PRs and require at least two consecutive failing runs before escalating.
